title: Selected Topics in Audiology
description: Intensive study in specific areas of audiology.

title: Hearing Science
description: Nature of sound and applications to hearing and speech, including acoustics, structure, and function of auditory system, and perception of sound.

title: Clinical Practice I
description: Applications of clinical procedures to patient assessment. Includes computer-based simulated cases, clinical observations, and supervised patient care involving diagnostics and hearing aid evaluations at the on-campus audiology clinic.

title: Clinical Methods Lab
description: Practice in tests and methods used in audiological clinical practicum.

title: Diagnostic Audiology I
description: Theoretical bases and technical experience necessary to perform basic audiologic assessment, including otoscopy, puretone, masking, speech, and immittance measures, testing and patient counseling. Hands-on experiences with different tests and equipment.

title: Hearing Amplification I
description: Hearing aid components and signal processing, electroacoustic analysis, prescriptive techniques, verification procedures, hearing aid orientation, follow-up and troubleshooting.

title: Audiologic Management
description: Examines audiology service delivery models including individual, group, community, interprofessional, and telepractice, applied to amplification, aural rehabilitation, verification/validation, counseling, and outcome measurement. Emphasizes patient-centered care, communication access, and quality improvement across clinical and community settings.

title: Research and Evidence-Based Practice in Audiology
description: Research methods and scientific writing in audiology/hearing science; critical evaluation of research; evidence-based practice in audiology; research proposal development.

title: Diagnostic Audiology II
description: Advanced procedures, including video-otoscopy, cerumen management, multiple component tympanometry, tests for 8th nerve, non-organic, and central involvement, and calibration. Principles and procedures for otoacoustic emission measurements (OAEs). Pathologies as they relate to audiologic measures.

title: Auditory Evoked Potentials I
description: Theoretical and clinical aspects of auditory evoked potentials, specifically otoacoustic emissions and their measurement, electrocochleography, and auditory brainstem responses.

title: Clinical Case Studies and Staffings I
description: Presentations and discussion of clinical cases and issues relative to clinical practice. Students’ clinical experiences are discussed relative to medical and audiological assessment and management.

title: Pediatric Audiology
description: Development of normal and abnormal auditory behavior, behavioral and physiological testing of infants and children, hearing screening for pre-and school-age children, educational audiology, auditory processing disorders, counseling of patient and family, and assistive listening devices.

title: Research Practicum
description: Participation in specific faculty research activities. Research methods and objectives of a specific research laboratory. Data collection and analysis.

title: Doctoral Special Studies
description: Individual study in field of specialization.

title: Advanced Evoked Potential Measures and Audiological Instrumentation
description: Advanced concepts and hands-on experience with different audiological instruments and measures to improve diagnostic skills in interpreting and performing behavioral and physiologic tests. Calibration instrumentation and techniques. Critical thinking, problem-solving, and reasoning skills pertaining to equipment testing parameters and use.

title: Clinical Practice II
description: Diagnostics and hearing aid evaluations/fittings in the on-campus audiology clinic.

title: Clinical Precepting in Audiology
description: Effective precepting, determining appropriate teaching styles to maximize clinical learning, including timely and positive feedback regarding clinical progress and assigning grades. Identifying need for remediation and developing effective programs to target deficient skills.

title: Seminar in Service Delivery Models in Audiology
description: Service delivery models in audiology, including 1:1 intervention, group treatment, community-based care, interprofessional collaborative practice, and telepractice.

title: Counseling and Communication in Audiology
description: Principles of culturally competent clinical communication for audiology care. Empathy, the four-habits model, shared decision making, trust. Methods from nursing and medicine. Discussion with parents of children with hearing loss and adults with audiology related concerns. In-class role play, reflection.

title: Communication Disorders Across Lifespan and Cultures
description: Communication processes and disorders from infancy to elderly, including phonetics, phonology, speech, and language. Prepares audiologists to recognize a variety of communication disorders, and to learn how to apply screening instruments, in culturally sensitive ways, and to make appropriate referrals.

title: Seminar in Contemporary Topics in Audiology and Hearing Science
description: Audiology and hearing science. Reading and critiquing journal articles and data emerging from research laboratories.

title: Field Clinical Practice
description: Supervised practicum in one or more approved community agencies.

title: Psychoacoustics
description: Psychophysical concepts underlying clinical audiology. Psychoacoustic abilities of individuals with normal hearing and sensorineural hearing loss. Practical experience in conducting psychoacoustic tests.

title: Hearing Conservation
description: Hearing conservation programs in various settings. Current research on occupational noise exposure and hearing loss and workers’ compensation coverage of hearing loss.

title: Externship in Audiology
description: Full-time clinical externship at approved agency. Continuation and intensification of clinical experiences with reduced amount of direct supervision culminating in ability to work independently.

title: On-Line Integrative Clinical Seminar
description: On-line discussion of clinical experiences and interesting cases.

title: Independent Research
description: Research in audiology or hearing science.

title: Doctoral Project
description: Individual investigation and preparation of the doctoral project for the audiology degree.
